current_bottleneck: 298a showed that sampling structural future embeddings improves daily-change KS and cross-cell structure, but hard nearest-neighbor decoding plus query anchoring still leaves unconditional level support wrong and long-horizon conditionality weak.
last_result_summary: 298a-v0 trained a conditional diagonal Gaussian over frozen 277d future embeddings and decoded samples through nearest training future paths. It scored 4/11: surface, block_ar, cointegration, and cross_cell_correlation passed; coverage, conditionality, time_series, regime_coverage, distributional_fidelity, mean_reversion, and pathwise_jump_realism failed. Change KS improved to 23/25, but level KS remained 1/25 and turb/calm width was only 1.043.
next_step_recommendation: Run a post-experiment interface analysis and then test 298b only if the bottleneck is hard nearest-neighbor structural decoding: keep the same learned embedding density, replace one-neighbor decode with a soft/mixture structural decoder over future-library paths, and do not add shells or bounded corrections.
current_best_model: 277d-v0, 279a-v0, 281a-v0, 281b-v0, 282b-v0, and 296c-v0 remain the current overall co-frontiers at 5/11.
current_best_note: 298a is cleaner than the fixed-center shell family but did not improve the frontier. Its useful evidence is mechanistic: stochastic structural embedding support repairs local change KS but not level KS or long-horizon conditionality under hard nearest-neighbor decoding.
